title: Data-Free On-Policy Distillation: How Far Can We Go Without External Data?
abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is increasingly applied to frontier foundation model post-training. Prior work in this area has largely focused on algorithmic advances, yet it remains unclear how much OPD depends on its training questions and, in particular, how far this dependence can be reduced. Across two representative single-teacher OPD settings, we find that training on 8 real prompts yields performance comparable to training on 17k problems, while datasets differing substantially in measured difficulty and initial distillation gap yield similar outcomes. Our analyses suggest two complementary explanations: repeated sampling could allow even a few prompts to expose substantial teacher supervision, while OPD transfers generalizable reasoning capabilities beyond dataset-specific knowledge. Building on these observations, we next propose a data-free on-policy distillation (DF-OPD) setting to investigate whether the system can supply the training questions itself, eliminating the need for external data. With 64 self-generated questions obtained without seed examples, DF-OPD yields performance comparable to full-data OPD in both single-teacher settings. This finding also holds in multi-teacher OPD: across mathematics, code, and instruction following, 1k generated questions achieve performance comparable to training on approximately 7k real post-training examples. We further explore whether OPD can operate even without explicit training questions. The experiments show that this is effective only in limited cases, where the student unexpectedly generates and answers its own questions, thereby reducing the process to an implicit form of DF-OPD. Together, these findings invite a reassessment of the role of training data in on-policy distillation. Code is available at this https URL

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Welcome to Advanced Methods in Language Model Training. Today's lecture is on a paper titled “Data-free On-policy Distillation” by researchers primarily from the Chinese Academy of Sciences and Tencent. We've seen a lot of recent work exploring on-policy distillation, with papers like "A Survey of On-Policy Distillation" trying to unify the concept. This paper takes a step back and asks a fundamental question: how much does the training data, the prompts themselves, actually matter for this process?
segments.zh: 欢迎来到语言模型训练进阶方法。今天要讲的论文是《无数据同策略蒸馏》，作者主要来自中国科学院和腾讯。最近有很多工作都在探索同策略蒸馏，比如《同策略蒸馏综述》就试图统一这个概念。这篇论文则退后一步，问了一个根本性的问题：训练数据，也就是那些提示词本身，对这个过程到底有多重要？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Yes, Noah?
segments.zh: 好的，诺亚？

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hi Professor. Could you quickly recap what makes this 'on-policy' as opposed to standard knowledge distillation? I want to make sure I have the baseline right.
segments.zh: 教授您好，您能快速概括一下，相比标准的知识蒸馏，这个方法为什么叫“同策略”吗？我想确认一下我对基线的理解是对的。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Of course. Standard distillation, or supervised fine-tuning, often uses a fixed dataset. The student learns to mimic the teacher's outputs on those specific examples. On-policy distillation, or OPD, is different. The student model generates its own responses, its own trajectories, and the teacher provides guidance at every step of that generation. It learns from states it actually encounters, which helps reduce the exposure bias you see when a model is trained on one data distribution but tested on its own, different distribution.
segments.zh: 当然可以。标准的蒸馏，或者说监督微调，通常用的是固定数据集。学生模型学着去模仿老师在这些特定样本上的输出。而在线策略蒸馏，也就是 OPD，就不一样了。学生模型自己生成回答，自己生成轨迹，老师则在生成的每一步提供指导。它从自己实际遇到的状态中学习，这有助于减少那种暴露偏差——就是模型在一个数据分布上训练，却在测试时面对自己产生的、不同的分布时会出现的问题。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Got it. So it’s more like reinforcement learning in that sense, learning from its own experience.
segments.zh: 明白了，所以从这个角度看，它更像是强化学习，从自己的经验中学习。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Exactly. OPD combines that on-policy aspect of RL with the dense, token-level supervision of distillation. The central contribution of this paper is to systematically test the data assumptions behind this method. The authors investigate how performance changes when you vary the number of training prompts, their difficulty, and even their domain. This has significant practical implications. If you don't need a massive, curated dataset, you can allocate resources elsewhere, like to more computation for student rollouts.
segments.zh: 没错。OPD把强化学习里那种同策略的特性，和蒸馏那种密集的、token级别的监督结合在了一起。这篇论文的核心贡献，就是系统地检验了这种方法背后的数据假设。作者研究了当你改变训练提示的数量、难度，甚至领域时，性能会怎么变化。这有很重要的实际意义。如果你不需要一个庞大的、精心筛选的数据集，就可以把资源分配到别的地方，比如给学生模型的轨迹多分配一些计算。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So what did they find? Is it data-hungry or not?
segments.zh: 那他们发现了什么呢？它到底是不是很吃数据？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Their findings suggest it is surprisingly data-efficient. This leads to their main proposal: Data-free On-policy Distillation, or DF-OPD. In this setup, they don't use any external prompts. Instead, they give the powerful teacher model a simple instruction, like 'write a math problem,' and use its generated questions as the prompts for distillation. There are no seed examples, no external databases, no quality filtering. The teacher creates its own curriculum, so to speak.
segments.zh: 他们的发现表明，它的数据效率高得出奇。这就引出了他们的核心方案：无数据同策略蒸馏，简称DF-OPD。在这个设定里，他们不用任何外部提示。而是给强大的教师模型一个简单的指令，比如“写一道数学题”，然后用它生成的问题作为蒸馏的提示。没有种子样本，没有外部数据库，也没有质量过滤。可以说，教师模型自己编排了一套课程。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Wait, so the teacher generates the questions, and then also provides the token-level guidance on those same questions?
segments.zh: 等等，所以老师既生成题目，又对同一批题目提供token级别的指导？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That's correct. The generated questions serve only as the starting point for the student's on-policy rollouts. The actual learning signal still comes from the teacher's token-by-token distributions as the student generates its answer.
segments.zh: 没错。生成的问题只是学生进行同策略轨迹的起点。真正的学习信号仍然来自学生生成答案时老师给出的逐token分布。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: To test this, they used a couple of setups, mainly focusing on math benchmarks. One was an RL-tuned teacher, and the other was simply a much larger model. The results were quite consistent. In one experiment, training on just eight prompts from the teacher's original dataset achieved a math score of 56.3, while training on the full 17,000-prompt dataset scored 56.4. The performance gain was almost entirely saturated with a tiny handful of examples.
segments.zh: 为了验证这一点，他们用了几种设置，主要聚焦在数学基准上。一个是经过强化学习调优的教师模型，另一个就是一个大得多的模型。结果相当一致。在一项实验中，只用教师原始数据集里的八个提示词训练，数学得分就达到了56.3，而用全部17000个提示词训练，得分是56.4。性能提升几乎在极少量样本下就已经完全饱和了。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hold on, only eight prompts? That seems too good to be true. How do they explain that? Does it just mean those eight prompts were perfectly chosen?
segments.zh: 等等，才八个提示词？这也好得有点不真实了吧。他们是怎么解释的？难道是说这八个提示词选得特别完美？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: They show it's not very sensitive to which eight prompts are chosen. Their explanation centers on the nature of on-policy sampling. The core unit of learning isn't the prompt, but the state encountered during a rollout. A single prompt can lead to many different student-generated sequences, and each token in those sequences is a new state, a new opportunity for the teacher to provide a correction. By repeatedly sampling from the same small set of prompts, the student still explores a vast state space. They find that rollout diversity is more important than prompt diversity.
segments.zh: 他们证明了选哪八个提示词其实影响不大。他们的解释核心在于同策略采样的本质。学习的基本单位不是提示词，而是轨迹过程中遇到的状态。一个提示词可以引出许多不同的学生生成序列，而这些序列中的每个token都是一个新状态，都是老师提供纠正的新机会。通过反复从同一小组提示词中采样，学生仍然在探索一个巨大的状态空间。他们发现轨迹的多样性比提示词的多样性更重要。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: That makes sense. So it's about exploring the student's policy space, not the prompt space. Did they see this hold up for out-of-domain data too?
segments.zh: 这就说得通了。所以关键在于探索学生的策略空间，而不是提示词空间。那他们在域外数据上也验证了这一点吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: They did. They trained a model on competitive programming problems and evaluated it on math benchmarks. The performance was nearly as good as training on in-domain math problems, recovering over 90 percent of the potential gain. This suggests that what's being transferred isn't necessarily factual knowledge about math, but a more general pattern of reasoning or behavior from the teacher model. And most notably, their data-free approach, using self-generated questions, often performed on par with, or even slightly better than, using the full, real dataset.
segments.zh: 确实做了。他们在竞赛编程问题上训练了一个模型，然后在数学基准上评估。表现几乎和在域内数学问题上训练一样好，恢复了超过90%的潜在增益。这说明被迁移的不一定是关于数学的事实性知识，而是来自教师模型的一种更通用的推理或行为模式。最值得注意的是，他们这种无数据的方法——用自己生成的问题——往往表现得和使用完整的真实数据集不相上下，甚至略好一些。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The implications here are significant. It challenges the conventional wisdom that you need a large, expensive, and carefully curated dataset for effective post-training. DF-OPD could make distillation much more accessible, especially when the teacher's original training data is proprietary. This is particularly useful in multi-teacher distillation. Instead of needing a large labeled dataset to route a prompt to the right domain-expert teacher—say, math, coding, or instruction-following—you just have each teacher generate its own prompts. The domain label is implicit.
segments.zh: 这里的意义很重大。它挑战了一个传统认知，也就是你需要一个庞大、昂贵且精心整理的数据集才能进行有效的后训练。DF-OPD 可以让蒸馏变得容易得多，尤其是当老师的原始训练数据是专有的时候。这在多教师蒸馏中特别有用。你不再需要一个大型标注数据集来把提示词路由到正确的领域专家教师，比如数学、编程或指令遵循，你只需要让每个教师生成自己的提示词就行。领域标签是隐含的。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Another question, a methodological one. The report mentioned the authors selected checkpoints based on performance on the evaluation benchmarks themselves. That seems like it could lead to an overestimation of the true performance, since there isn't a separate validation set.
segments.zh: 还有一个问题，是关于方法论的。报告里提到，作者是根据模型在评估基准本身上的表现来选择检查点的。这看起来可能会导致对真实性能的高估，因为并没有一个单独的验证集。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That's a very sharp and important critique. The authors acknowledge this is a limitation and frame the paper as a work in progress. This practice can indeed inflate scores, so the absolute numbers should be interpreted with caution. Independent replication with a proper validation set for model selection would be necessary to fully confirm the magnitude of these results. It also doesn't address potential pitfalls, like the teacher reproducing its own biases or blind spots in the self-generated data.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常犀利且重要的批评。作者也承认这是一个局限，并把论文定位为一项进行中的工作。这种做法确实可能抬高分数，所以那些绝对数值应该谨慎解读。要想完全确认这些结果的量级，还需要有独立复现，并且在模型选择时使用一个合适的验证集。这也没有解决一些潜在的隐患，比如教师模型在自生成数据中复制自身的偏见或盲点。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Right. So the principle is promising, but the specific numbers need more validation.
segments.zh: 对，所以这个原理是很有前景的，但具体的数字还需要更多验证。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Precisely. The key takeaway is not about hitting a specific benchmark score, but about shifting our perspective on what drives learning in on-policy distillation. The evidence suggests that the richness of the on-policy interaction, driven by repeated student rollouts, can compensate for a lack of diversity in the initial prompts. This makes methods like Data-free On-policy Distillation a very practical and compelling direction for future work in model alignment and transfer learning.
segments.zh: 正是如此。关键不在于达到某个具体的基准分数，而在于转变我们对在线策略蒸馏中学习驱动因素的看法。证据表明，由学生模型反复生成轨迹所带来的丰富的在线策略交互，可以弥补初始提示缺乏多样性的问题。这使得无数据在线策略蒸馏这类方法成为模型对齐和迁移学习未来研究中一个非常实用且有吸引力的方向。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 感谢收听。如果还有任何问题，可以问我们的人工智能助手，或者留言评论。
